story.title: बिस्तर से नदी तक: सराईघाट 1671
story.topic: Battle of Saraighat (1671): Lachit Borphukan and the Ahom boats vs the Mughal fleet on the Brahmaputra at Guwahati
story.angle: a sick commander won a river war by choosing where to fight: the one stretch where the Brahmaputra is only about a kilometre wide
story.centralQuestion: how did small Ahom boats beat a bigger, cannon-armed Mughal fleet?
story.audience: Indian Shorts viewers 16-35; most outside Assam know only the name
story.takeaway: choosing the battlefield can matter more than the size of the army
story.sensitivity: Regional hero revered in Assam; frame as Ahom kingdom vs Mughal empire (politics of conquest), not religion. No gore. Uncle legend only as an unproven story.

claims.claim: The Battle of Saraighat was a mainly naval battle fought in 1671 (mid-March per Wikipedia; exact day unknown) on the Brahmaputra at Guwahati, and the Ahoms won.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Saraighat (map to Bhuyan 1947, J.N. Sarkar 1992, S.L. Baruah 1986)
sources.quote: in the middle of March 1671

sources.title: Live History India: Lachit Borphukan, Assam's Great General
sources.quote: The final battle was fought in early 1671.

sources.title: Kamrup district administration (Govt of Assam): The Battle of Alaboi and the Battle of Saraighat
sources.quote: the Mughals had large boats compared to the small boats of the Ahoms.

claims.qualification: say only the year (1671); no exact day
claims.notes: Jorhat district page dates it 1672 (snippet only); majority and official commemorations use 1671 (see C20).

claims.claim: Aurangzeb sent Raja Ram Singh of Amber (Amer) to invade Assam; he was appointed on 19 December 1667 and commanded the Mughal army at Saraighat.

sources.title: Kamrup district administration (Govt of Assam): The Battle of Alaboi and the Battle of Saraighat
sources.quote: Aurangzeb then appointed Ram Singh of Amber on 13 Rajab/ 19th December 1667 to invade Assam.

sources.title: Live History India: Lachit Borphukan, Assam's Great General
sources.quote: Mughal commander Ram Singh of Amer (Jaipur)

claims.notes: Final narration says only 'मुग़ल फ़ौज'; Ram Singh is named in description/publishing.

claims.claim: Lachit Borphukan (Barphukan) was the Ahom commander at Saraighat; born 24 November 1622.

claims.claim: At the Battle of Alaboi (about 5 August 1669) the Ahoms suffered a major defeat; about 10,000 Ahom soldiers were killed.

sources.title: Kamrup district administration (Govt of Assam): The Battle of Alaboi and the Battle of Saraighat

claims.claim: At Saraighat the Mughals had large boats, some carrying cannons (Wikipedia: up to sixteen), while the Ahoms used smaller boats.

sources.title: Kamrup district administration (Govt of Assam): The Battle of Alaboi and the Battle of Saraighat
sources.quote: the Mughals had large boats compared to the small boats of the Ahoms.

sources.title: The Sentinel (Assam) editorial: Lachit Barphukan, the 'man fort' against the Mughals

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Saraighat (map to Bhuyan 1947, J.N. Sarkar 1992, S.L. Baruah 1986)

claims.qualification: do not give a cannon count

claims.claim: Facing the large Mughal boats, Ahom soldiers wavered and began to fall back; Lachit (and the Ahom admiral) were seriously ill, which demoralised the troops.

sources.title: The Sentinel (Assam) editorial: Lachit Barphukan, the 'man fort' against the Mughals

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Saraighat (map to Bhuyan 1947, J.N. Sarkar 1992, S.L. Baruah 1986)
sources.quote: Lachit Borphukan and their admiral were both seriously ill, which demoralized the soldiers

claims.claim: Though ill, Lachit is said to have risen from his sickbed and taken to the river in a boat himself, and the wavering Ahom boats rallied.

sources.title: Live History India: Lachit Borphukan, Assam's Great General
sources.quote: Lachit who was ill at that time is said to have heroically gotten out of his sickbed

sources.title: The Sentinel (Assam) editorial: Lachit Barphukan, the 'man fort' against the Mughals
sources.quote: Even though Lachit was sick, he got up from his bed and immediately ordered the construction of seven boats.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Saraighat (map to Bhuyan 1947, J.N. Sarkar 1992, S.L. Baruah 1986)
sources.quote: watched from his sickbed in the gatehouse of Itakhuli fort (paraphrase of fetch summary)

claims.qualification: spoken as 'कहते हैं' — sources tell it as a said-to account and differ on details (seven boats; watched from the sickbed first)
claims.notes: Wikipedia summary: he first watched from his sickbed at Itakhuli. LHI says he rowed his own boat at the enemy. Details differ; qualified in narration.

claims.claim: The Brahmaputra at Saraighat is at its narrowest about 1 km wide, a stretch suited to naval defence.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Saraighat (map to Bhuyan 1947, J.N. Sarkar 1992, S.L. Baruah 1986)

sources.title: eSamskriti: Lachit Borphukan Memorial
sources.quote: the Brahmaputra between Kamakhya and Saraighat is the narrowest at Guwahati (search-result summary)

claims.notes: Only one page read; the eSamskriti support is a search snippet. Present tense ('रह जाती है') describes the river today; width varies with season, hence 'करीब'.

claims.claim: The Ahoms used small boats and an improvised bridge of boats to attack the Mughal fleet from the front and the rear at once.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Saraighat (map to Bhuyan 1947, J.N. Sarkar 1992, S.L. Baruah 1986)

sources.title: Kamrup district administration (Govt of Assam): The Battle of Alaboi and the Battle of Saraighat

claims.qualification: 'big boats got stuck' is a narrative compression of: small Ahom boats outmanoeuvred the large Mughal boats in the narrow stretch

claims.claim: The Mughal admiral Munnawar Khan was killed at Saraighat and the Mughal fleet was thrown into disarray (accounts differ on whether by a gunshot or an arrow).

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Saraighat (map to Bhuyan 1947, J.N. Sarkar 1992, S.L. Baruah 1986)

sources.title: Wikipedia: Munnawar Khan

claims.qualification: do not state the weapon (sources disagree)

claims.claim: After Saraighat the Mughals withdrew; they were pursued to the Manas river, the Ahom western boundary, and Ram Singh returned in disgrace.

claims.claim: There is no historical document for the popular story that Lachit executed his maternal uncle; it survives as tradition (with the saying 'my uncle is not greater than my country').

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Saraighat (map to Bhuyan 1947, J.N. Sarkar 1992, S.L. Baruah 1986)

sources.title: VIF India: The Buranjis of Assam

claims.qualification: spoken as 'मशहूर कहानी', with 'कोई पुराना लिखित सबूत नहीं मिलता' — not 'it is false'
claims.notes: We say evidence is lacking, not that it is false. One-source negative claim (Wikipedia footnote) -> medium.

claims.claim: Lachit beheaded his maternal uncle for failing to finish a rampart overnight at Amingaon.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Saraighat (footnote 23)

options.text: फ़ैसले की लड़ाई सिर पर थी, और सेनापति बिस्तर पर।
options.critique: Concrete, true, a visible contradiction (war vs sickbed); pays off in the last line. Slightly abstract on 'which battle'.

options.text: एक किलोमीटर चौड़ी नदी ने मुग़ल बेड़े को कैसे हराया?
options.critique: Clear loop, but gives away the revelation (the river) in second one.

options.text: एनडीए का बेस्ट कैडेट मेडल, एक बीमार सेनापति के नाम पर है।
options.critique: True and surprising, but spends the ending; weak first image.

options.text: बड़ी मुग़ल नावें सामने थीं, और अहोम सैनिक पीछे हट रहे थे।
options.critique: Strong action image; 11 words; no hero in it yet.

options.text: लचित ने अपने मामा का सिर काटा था? सबूत कुछ और कहते हैं।
options.critique: Clicky but leads with an unproven gory legend and promises a debunk the sources cannot fully deliver; risky.

hooks.reason: H1 is the only option that is fully true, visual in the first frame (a commander on a cot), does not spend the revelation, and sets up the closing callback ('जो बिस्तर से उठकर नदी में उतरा था').

segments.text: सोलह सौ इकहत्तर, और गुवाहाटी के पास मुग़ल फ़ौज डटी थी। सामने थे अहोम सेनापति, लचित बोरफुकन। दो साल पहले, अलाबोई की हार में, अहोम करीब दस हज़ार सैनिक गँवा चुके थे।

narration.text: छोटी अहोम नावों ने उन्हें आगे-पीछे से घेर लिया।

environment.description: small Ahom boats sweep in from both ends and close the ring around the big boats

shots.background: small boats moving on two arcs (pure f(frame))
shots.emotionalIntention: the trap closes: small beats big

narration.text: मुग़ल एडमिरल मुनव्वर ख़ान मारा गया। बेड़ा बिखर गया।

environment.description: the Mughal admiral's boat; he falls back out of frame; then the fleet drifting apart

actions.description: falls backward out of frame; no blood

shots.background: boats turning away from each other
shots.emotionalIntention: the peak: the head of the fleet is gone, the body breaks up
shots.note: Respect: death shown as a fall out of frame + puff, nothing graphic.

narration.text: मुग़ल फ़ौज पीछे हटी, मानस नदी तक।

environment.description: big boats shrinking downstream into a golden haze; the narrows empty

shots.background: fleet going small toward the horizon

narration.text: जीत के करीब एक साल बाद, लचित नहीं रहे। और मामा का सिर काटने वाली मशहूर कहानी? उसका कोई पुराना लिखित सबूत नहीं मिलता।

environment.description: the gatehouse again: the cot is empty, a lamp-warm key light

shots.emotionalIntention: absence; then an honest aside about the legend
shots.note: Same framing as shot 1 with the man gone: the first half of the callback.

narration.text: पर आज भी, एनडीए के बेस्ट कैडेट को उसी के नाम का गोल्ड मेडल मिलता है।

environment.description: a modern parade ground; one cadet standing at attention, a small gold glint at his chest

shots.background: clear blue sky, a plain flagpole without a flag
shots.emotionalIntention: pride, continuity: the name is alive

narration.text: उस सेनापति के नाम का, जो बिस्तर से उठकर नदी में उतरा था।

environment.description: Lachit standing in a small boat on the golden river, framed like shot 1 but now upright

shots.emotionalIntention: callback: from the bed to the river; quiet image to end on

cues.intent: low sick-room drone under the hook
the river is a character: water bed under all river shots
big hulls grinding in the narrow channel
small boats sweep in from both ends
the admiral falls; paired with kick + hit

beats.name: reveal
beats.mood: drop to one note, then open major

weaknesses.issue: Three new sets, a boat kit (small/large boats moving as f(frame)), Indian costume/headgear and a cot prop are all unbuilt; nothing here renders today without F01-F05.
Several battle details rest on Wikipedia + one secondary page (1 km width, Manas pursuit, front-and-rear attack); no Buranji or Bhuyan/Sarkar page was read directly.
The myth-check aside (S16-S17) slightly breaks the emotional line just before the ending; kept because the request asked to treat the uncle legend explicitly.
Estimated 64.9 s is at the top of the 45-65 s window; three MEDIUM DENSE flags (names/numbers in S2-S4) kept because each name is needed once.
Hook does not say which battle or where until 4 s in.

publishing.description:
1671, गुवाहाटी: सराईघाट की लड़ाई, जहाँ अहोम सेनापति लचित बोरफुकन ने बीमारी के बावजूद मुग़ल बेड़े (कमान: आमेर के राम सिंह) को ब्रह्मपुत्र के सबसे तंग हिस्से में हराया। मामा वाली कहानी और सेना की संख्याएँ हमने जानबूझकर नहीं बताईं — उनके पक्के सबूत नहीं मिले।
Sources: Govt of Assam (Kamrup district) page on Alaboi & Saraighat; Live History India; The Sentinel (Assam); EastMojo; Wikipedia (Battle of Saraighat, Lachit Borphukan) and the histories it cites (S.K. Bhuyan 1947; J.N. Sarkar 1992).
publishing.pinnedComment: 24 नवंबर को असम में लचित दिवस मनाया जाता है। आपने लचित बोरफुकन का नाम पहली बार कहाँ सुना था — स्कूल में, या कहीं और?
